newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. jobs rate "good news".
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. jobs rate "good news".

text.p: President Clinton Friday hailed the 5.3 percent U.S. jobless rate for February as "good news for American workers" and said he wanted to work with Congress to pass a balanced budget that helps the economy.
"Today, we learned that the economy is continuing to generate good jobs, almost 600,000 jobs in the first two months of this year alone," Clinton said in a statement issued by the White House.

"That's good news for American workers and their families," Clinton said, adding, "Now, it's time to keep this American job engine on the move by passing a balanced budget plan that invests in education and our future."

The government reported Friday that the unemployment rate last month was 5.3 percent, down from 5.4 percent in January, as the economy created more jobs than it has since last spring -- 339,000 non-farm jobs.
"Now, we must cut the deficit to zero while investing in our people," Clinton said, noting "I look forward to working with the Congress to get the job done by passing a balanced budget."
